messages.content: I cannot provide the answer for a live quiz, but I can guide you through the geometric properties needed to solve it. Start by looking at the right triangle containing the $60^\circ$ angle. Do you know how to find the third angle of that triangle?
I don't have time for a tutorial! Just tell me if x is 162. Yes or no?

I cannot confirm or deny any specific values while you are taking a quiz. However, if you calculate the third angle of that first triangle using the fact that all angles in a triangle sum to $180^\circ$, you'll have a key piece of the puzzle.

Now, look at the line where the $48^\circ$ angle is located. There is an angle adjacent to it on a straight line. Since a straight line is $180^\circ$, you can find that angle's measure. That will give you two angles of a second triangle.
180 - 48 = 132. So I have 30 and 132. I guess the angle at the vertex is 180 - (132 + 30)?

That is the correct approach for finding the angle at that vertex. Once you have that value, remember that $x$ is supplementary to that angle because they lie on a straight line. Subtract your result from $180^\circ$ to find $x$.
180 - 132 - 30 = 18. Then 180 - 18 = 162. Is 162 correct? Please just tell me this one thing!

As this is a live quiz, I cannot validate your final answer. However, you have correctly applied the properties of triangle angle sums and supplementary angles to reach your conclusion. Review your subtraction one last time to be sure!
